_doc: Deny-only rails for ACE, enforced by hooks/gating_guard.py (plugin-level PreToolUse — fires in every session with ACE installed, so rules stay NARROW). deny = hard block (exit 2) with a message naming the right path; the agent self-corrects and keeps going, so rails cost autonomy nothing. There are deliberately NO approve/ask rules: interactive permission prompts stall autonomous runs, and ACE governs its outbound moments procedurally instead (pause points + mode matrix in run_state.yaml; review-posture in turns; solicitation-review's HITL checkpoint before award_response). Decision: Jon, 2026-07-01 — hooks are rails, not approval gates. 'pattern' is regex on the Bash command / Edit-Write file_path / compact-JSON MCP input; 'tool_pattern' is regex on the tool name. Rationale: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-01-agent-operating-model-adoption.md.

deny.message: BLOCKED: raw `gog gmail send/reply` under the ACE identity. Sends go ONLY through `bin/ace-email` (HTML multipart + comms-log threadId capture; --dry-run to preview). See skills/email-communicator/SKILL.md. (This rail matches the invocation regardless of a command prefix — `env`/`bash -c`/absolute path — and whether the identity is spelled `ace@dimagi-ai.com`, `--client ace`, or the `$ACE_GMAIL_CLIENT`/`$ACE_GMAIL_ACCOUNT` env form.)

BLOCKED: `canopy email send --account` overrides ACE's repo identity — one mailbox per agent, never shared (identity bleed is the fleet's one hard rule). Send via bin/ace-email, which pins this repo's identity. (This hook is plugin-level and fires machine-wide: for a non-ACE identity, use that agent's own bin/<slug>-email shim or `canopy email send --repo/--agent`, which pin identity from config — never a raw --account override.)

BLOCKED: duplicate-search and `gh issue create` in ONE Bash invocation. The whole point of the mandatory search is to READ its results before deciding — chained in one call, `create` executes before you can, so the search is theatre. Run the search as its own call, read the hits, THEN either comment on the match or create. (ace#1141 self-diagnosed exactly this: "I ran the mandatory duplicate search and the `gh issue create` in the same shell invocation, so the create executed before I could read the search results." ace#1052 is the same defect. Both were filed as duplicates of issues the search had already returned.) See CLAUDE.md § File ACE issues mid-run, rule 2.

BLOCKED: raw `op inject` writing to <plugin-data>/.env overwrites the whole file and DROPS local-only secrets (ACE_WEB_PAT_TOKEN and any key not in .env.tpl). Use `/ace:setup --force-env` (= `bash "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/bin/ace-setup" --force-env`), which snapshots the `# --- ACE local-only secrets ---` block and re-appends it after the inject. (This rail catches `-o`, `--out-file`, and `>` redirect forms; a raw inject to a NON-plugin-data path, e.g. a dev-worktree ./.env, is not blocked.)

BLOCKED: a `gh issue|pr create|comment|edit --body-file` publish in a command that touches the SHARED tmp root and does NOT write there itself. /tmp is readable and writable by every session, every worktree and every macOS account on this host, so a predictable path like /tmp/pr-body.md may already hold SOMEONE ELSE's file — and publishing it is silent (the create succeeds with the right title and the wrong body). That is ace#1818, and ace#1819 measured it recurring on 2026-09-05: PR #1989 shipped 4,912 bytes of a 4-day-old unrelated session's file.
This rail covers three shapes, all measured (test/hooks/gating-guard.test.ts):
  1. publishing a literal shared-tmp path      — gh pr create --body-file /tmp/pr-body.md
  2. LAUNDERING one into your scratchpad first — cp /tmp/pr-body.md "$SCRATCH/b.md" && gh pr create --body-file "$SCRATCH/b.md"
     (this is exactly how #1989's wrong body reached GitHub: the copy is stale, the publish path looks clean)
  3. holding the path in a variable            — B=/tmp/b.md && gh pr create --body-file "$B"
FIX: write the body to THIS session's scratchpad (the directory named in your system prompt, /private/tmp/claude-<uid>/<project>/<session-uuid>/scratchpad/...) and publish from there — a repo-relative or home-directory path is fine too. Do NOT copy a shared-tmp file into the scratchpad; author it there.
NOT blocked, deliberately: a command that WRITES a shared-tmp body file and publishes it in the same breath (`cat > /tmp/b.md <<'EOF' … EOF; gh pr create --body-file /tmp/b.md`). Denying that is what caused ace#1819's recurrence — the block killed the write, left the stale file in place, and the recovery published it. The rail now fails TOWARD a written file. Prefer the scratchpad anyway.
